newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Tuesday were seen mixed, with strength seen in Illinois on strong local packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Illinois hogs were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, with top prices at the plant expected to range $57.00-$57.50.
Indiana/Ohio hogs were expected steady to $0.50 lower, with a top of $57.50 to $58.00 for hogs delivered to the plant, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hogs at the plant were called steady to weak and could range $58.00 to $58.50.

Many packers continued to work reduced shifts in an effort to stabilize soft operating margins, dealers and packer buyers said. Slaughter cutbacks were initiated last Monday amid sluggish pork demand and higher cash hog prices.

Pork demand remained light at midday, with 17.5 loads of pork cuts and 6.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold at steady to slightly higher prices, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot pork report.
Marketings also continued light as farmers concentrated on field preparation and corn planting from Iowa to Ohio, dealers said.
